stem: A child with neutropaenia now also has low haemoglobin and low platelets; what is the best interpretation of this result pattern?

options.text: The problem should no longer be treated as an isolated single-cell-line abnormality
The new results make benign ethnic neutropaenia the most likely explanation
The white cell result can now be ignored because the main issue is platelet count
This change is expected in all children with viral suppression

explanation: The correct interpretation is that this is no longer an isolated single-cell-line abnormality. When neutropaenia is accompanied by anaemia and thrombocytopaenia, the pattern suggests involvement of more than one cell line and should be assessed accordingly.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: WBC Disorders

rationale: Multi-line cytopenia changes the interpretation of neutropaenia and should prompt review of the full blood count rather than focusing on one abnormal result.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the presence of low haemoglobin and low platelets means the abnormality is no longer confined to a single cell line.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because benign ethnic neutropaenia explains isolated neutropaenia, not additional anaemia and thrombocytopaenia.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because reactive lymphocytosis is a different white cell pattern and does not account for the other cytopenias.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the neutropaenia still matters and multiple cell lines need to be considered together.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because viral suppression can cause neutropaenia, but this broader pattern is not expected in all children with viral illness.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
